searchText: <dannyryan> Isnt there another way to do this? You can take a recent deposit proof from the beacon chain to construct the right-most branch of the deposit tree and then just add deposits from there from the more recent EL history <dannyryan> The rightmost branch is also in the dep contract <dannyryan> But if this were to be spec'd it *might* live with the ws stuff in the CL spec but I personally think more appropriate to live in an eip, similar to slashing db standard and other things BUT there is a diversity of opinion here... <dannyryan> And for reference, the discussions at amphora about breaking the log promise has manifested as eip 4444 and discussions around that > right most branch This is what I meant by "the deposit Merkle tree can be significantly compressed" - because the implementation I just wrote only stores the right most branch of the finalized tree + pending deposits <dannyryan> Gotcha, but I question whether that branch needs to be disseminated during ws sync <dannyryan> And what needs to be transmitted in the beacon api? Does pulling the merkle branch from a block involve assumptions about deposit activity? I was transmitting the branch via an API endpoint <dannyryan> Indeed. Pulling it from the dep contract is more failsafe <dannyryan> Ah, assuming a ws provider would serve that endpoint to a bootstrapping node? I see (re @merge_chat_bot: <ethDreamer> I was transmitting the branch via an API endpoint) Yes. Correct me if I'm wrong but the deposit contract can only serve the branch of the latest tree at the head of the chain - which is nearly always going to be different than the tree as it was at the finalized checkpoint <dannyryan> Right but you can sync to the head, then grab the branch and be able to build deposits from there, no? <dannyryan> And if this or something like it does manifest as just a beacon api endpoint, that along with a quick note in the cl ws specs might be sufficient You need the right-most branch of the deposit contract at ws checkpoint - otherwise you can't verify Merkle proofs of deposits between the checkpoint and the head when you start syncing Unless I'm missing something.. You can verify deposits in beacon blocks without any external data - you don't need an eth1 node at all to verify the beacon chain. (well, that is assuming you have the genesis state or some other checkpoint state But can you construct proofs for block proposals with deposits between the checkpoint and head when you started syncing? <dannyryan> The deposits are constructed by each proposer and contain proofs <dannyryan> See Deposit data structure <dannyryan> So verifying the beacon chain is just a matter of verifying those proofs <dannyryan> Whereas constructing it requires knowing recent deposit logs and rightmost merkle branch <dannyryan> And dep logs will be available within ws period because any 4444 like proposal will almost certainly only prune outside of longest ws period Rightmost branch *before* the deposit you're constructing the proof for though <dannyryan> Hmm right so you need a depth of pending_deposits rightmost branch I mean the data structure we came up with was: DepositTreeSnapshot { branch: Vector[Hash32], deposits: uint64, eth1_block_hash: Hash32, } Though hash could be swapped out with height.. <dannyryan> So one thing that doesnt work with any of these ws bound methods is if deposit queue is deeper than 4444 pruning period but if pruning period is 4 months or a year, thats quite an exceptional case <dannyryan> Right, makes sense (re @merge_chat_bot: <ethDreamer> I mean the data structure we came up with was: DepositTreeSnapshot { branch: Vector[Hash32], deposits: uint64, eth1_block_hash: Hash32, } Though hash could be swapped out with height..) <dannyryan> I'd love to avoid needing another endpoint to bootstrap this but... the arbitrary depth of the rightmost branch of the earliest pending deposit (rather than the heas) is annoying You need more than the depth though. You need the whole branch at the ws checkpoint. Without them you can't construct proofs for deposits just after the checkpoint but before the point you started syncing (if you only have the branch from the deposit contract at the head). As each deposit between the checkpoint and the head will change the lower hashes in the branch <dannyryan> I meant a rightmost branch at an arbitrary depth in the chain <dannyryan> Hmm so if you backfill blocks to 4 months (which you should as per spec), you can get the rightmost branch assuming 1 deposit in that period Not sure if that is a reasonable assumption <dannyryan> And you dont need the rightmost branch at the ws checkpoint (although this will suffice). You need the rightmost branch of the latest not yet included deposit. But I think we agree there If there wasn't a deposit in that period, wouldn't the current right most branch work as it would be the same? It seems like you'd need to have a deposit that hadn't been included for 4 months. It would be nice to avoid adding backfill as a dependency on block production. Slightly tangential, but you can quite nicely prove that some right branch is the latest (rightmost) branch against the beacon state eth1_data. It’s nice API consumers could verify that. <dannyryan> Ah right (re @merge_chat_bot: <Adrian Sutton> If there wasn't a deposit in that period, wouldn't the current right most branch work as it would be the same? It seems like you'd need to have a deposit that hadn't been included for 4 months.) <dannyryan> So you can get it either from a dep in that range or the current read of the contract <dannyryan> Might be an edge case if eth1data voting has stalled out for a long time <dannyryan> Dropping that and stepping away to chill on the new year. Happy new year!
